w1.title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
w1.summary: MoEngage built Merlin AI, a set of AI agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that let marketing and product teams draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns from a single conversation. Learn how MoEngage turned its existing APIs into MCP tools and kept each tenant's data isolated while giving agents secure access to live platform data.

w2.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform
w2.summary: Legacy mainframe Assembler applications are costly to maintain and hard to staff. This post presents a multi-stage, AI-powered methodology using Amazon Bedrock, Kiro IDE, and AWS Transform to extract business rules, convert Assembler through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized Java Spring Boot applications on AWS.

w3.title: Novo Nordisk modernizes manufacturing process documents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
w3.summary: Novo Nordisk's Manufacturing Technology team within the Tablet area team built a process-intelligence assistant on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using a GraphRAG architecture that pairs a knowledge graph in Amazon Neptune with hybrid search in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless to turn millions of controlled manufacturing documents into grounded, cited answers.

w4.title: Mitigate memory price increases with components harvested from retiring devices
w4.summary: The circular economy just picked up one of its strongest business cases yet, and it didn’t come from a sustainability mandate. It came from a memory shortage. An AI-induced memory shortage has pushed the price of new devices up, causing organizations to recalculate their repair-vs-replace threshold, and to look again at what a decommissioned device is still worth. Rather than proceeding with typical 3 to 4-year refresh cycles, many IT and procurement teams have shifted to preservation mode, hold

w5.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
w5.summary: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so agentic retrieval can answer questions over CSV, XLSX, and XLS files. It looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row, then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer multi-step analytical questions.

w6.title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
w6.summary: With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail matches by meaning rather than keyword, which can block more than you intend. This post presents eight best practices for writing a topic precisely enough that the guardrail blocks what you mean and passes what you don't.

w7.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock
w7.summary: Many generative AI applications resend the same long context on every request. Prompt caching lets open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock reuse it to reduce input cost and latency. This post shows implicit and explicit caching through the Chat Completions API and applies caching to an OpenCode coding agent session.

w10.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1
w10.summary: GS Caltex connects Amazon SageMaker Canvas to Amazon SageMaker Pipelines so process engineers' no-code models run in production. This post shows how ML engineers reuse validated preprocessing flows and models, cutting deployment from about a week to a few hours and running batch inference every 30 minutes.

w11.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
w11.summary: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines.

w12.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
w12.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request.

w13.title: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures
w13.summary: Deploy OpenFold3-preview from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to predict 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, and ligand complexes in your own AWS account. The post covers asynchronous inference, multi-GPU parallelism, bringing your own MSAs for accuracy and privacy, and scaling to zero to reduce cost.

w14.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot
w14.summary: Learn how AssemblyAI runs cost-optimized speech-to-text inference at scale on AWS, using Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an Amazon SQS-based retry architecture to achieve 70% cost savings while maintaining SLA commitments across European Regions.

w15.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
w15.summary: Amazon Bedrock provides built-in, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that made it. This post shows how to attribute per-user Bedrock costs for AI developer and productivity tools using IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0, and how to enforce per-user usage limits.
